messages:
oncall-bot: Incident detected: spike in KV cache write amplification + continuous-batching latency for customer cohort. Alert: kv_cache_write_rate up 12x, batch_latency P95 > 2.5s. Affected region: us-west-2.

oncall-bot: Pager routed to sana. Priority: Sev2.

sana: I'm on it. Looking at dashboards now — seeing a sharp increase in kv cache size and OOM GC pressure on several hosts in the batch pool.

mike: fyi I just saw error logs from batch-worker-12: `kv_cache: failed to alloc page: out of memory` repeating. Could be cache blowup due to missing eviction on a new prefix pattern.

deepa: Any customer-impact notes yet?

clarence: Customer-ops: we have two customers with high request volume (acme-corp, beta-platform) showing elevated request errors ~5%. No full outages but increased 5xx and slow tails.

sana: Ok — immediate goal: reduce cache write pressure and slow the batching pipeline. Plan: 1) flip batching_v2 feature flag to conservative canary (5% traffic) 2) enable per-customer override to throttle batch size for acme-corp and beta-platform 3) temporarily disable kv_prefix_caching for non-prod suffixes.

mike: How do we flip the flag safely? Can we do a percent rollout via flags service?

sana: Yes. Command: `flagsctl set batching_v2 rollout_percent=5 target=all` (will route 5% of requests through new batching). We'll monitor kv_write_rate and batch_latency for 10m.

deepa: I'll prepare the per-customer override: `flagsctl set batching_v2 override customer=acme-corp batch_max_tokens=32` then same for beta-platform. That should reduce batch sizes and writes.

ryan: I'll stand up checksum/tracing on the affected batch-workers to confirm KV prefix churn. Pushing a short-lived logging patch to staging then to canary.

oncall-bot: action required: please ack and post status updates every 10 minutes.

clarence: customer-ops — starting outreach: pinging both account teams and logging tickets.

sana: Executing step 1 now: flipping rollout to 5%.

mike: saw the rollout. Metrics: kv_write_rate dropped ~22% on canary nodes, P95 latency for canary down ~350ms. No errors yet.

deepa: Applying per-customer override for acme-corp now. Command: `flagsctl set batching_v2 override customer=acme-corp batch_max_tokens=32 --note "emergency per-cust throttle"`

clarence: Acme account team: they confirm a reduction in 5xxs observed on their side (via their telemetry).

sana: Good. Apply same override for beta-platform.

mike: Beta-platform override applied. Observed similar drop in their error rate.

deepa: Also toggled `kv_prefix_caching` off for non-prod keys with `prefix_exempt=~"^stg_|^dev_"` to stop noise from internal test traffic.

ryan: Logs show a few hot key prefixes causing repeated full-key writes — I'll add a short-term dedupe on writes for identical consecutive prefixes in the canary path. Patching live in 5m.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: canary-deploy/kv-write-dedupe started by ryan.

mike: After dedupe patch, observed kv_write_rate further reduced ~35% on canary nodes. Batch latency P95 trending down to baseline.

clarence: Customer-ops: acme and beta-platform report improved latency; both say degraded but acceptable. No new pager escalations from them.

sana: Given positive canary signals, next step: expand rollout to 25% for another 10m, then to 50% if stable. We'll keep per-customer overrides in place until we confirm system-wide stability.

deepa: Agreed. I'll also prepare a short-lived per-customer override script to quickly revert if we see instability: `flagsctl unset batching_v2 override customer=$CUST` saved in incident playbook.

ryan: Monitors to watch: kv_cache_write_rate (cluster), batch_latency_p95 (service), host_gc_count, error_rate_by_customer. I added an alert threshold: batch_latency_p95 > 1.5s after expansion triggers auto-rollback via runbook.

oncall-bot: action: scheduled escalation check-in in 10m.

--- 10 minutes later ---

sana: Expanding to 25% now.

mike: Metrics look ok in the first 3m; canary and 25% nodes holding. kv_write_rate remains down ~28% overall.

clarence: Customer-ops: pushing update to account teams: we expect gradual improvement; will keep them updated.

deepa: Reminder: keep per-customer overrides on for acme and beta-platform until we reach 50%. They have the most traffic and were the highest error contributors.

ryan: Noted. Also, I'm seeing a small uptick in write latency on a single host — investigating IO queue depth, might be unrelated.

mike: If that host degrades, we'll exclude it from batch pool via `poolctl drain host=batch-worker-42`.

noncall-bot: deploy-bot: canary-deploy/kv-write-dedupe finished successfully.

--- 20 minutes after start ---

sana: Rolling to 50% now. Monitoring closely.

mike: 50% ramp completed. System-wide metrics near baseline; error rate down to pre-incident levels for most customers.

clarence: Acme and beta-platform confirm their side is stable. No additional customer impact reported.

deepa: Keeping per-cust overrides until end of incident. We'll remove them as part of controlled rollback after full stabilisation.

sana: Handoff notes for next oncall (ryan takes over in 45m): 1) Incident: KV cache write amplification due to new prefix pattern + batching_v2 defaults that allowed large batches 2) Mitigations: conservative feature-flag canary, per-customer batch_max_tokens overrides, disable non-prod prefix caching, kv-write dedupe patch 3) Current state: normalizing; rollout at 50% with overrides active; monitors green 4) Actions for follow-up: postmortem, permanent fix to eviction heuristics, add a canary test for hot-prefix detection, consider default batch_max_tokens reduction.

ryan: Ack. I'll take the handoff. Will keep an eye for host IO issue and revert per-customer overrides once rollout has sat at 50% for 30m and metrics stable.

clarence: Customer-ops: closing urgent outreach loop; will keep high-touch until full rollback of overrides.

oncall-bot: Incident update: Severity reduced to Sev3. Next scheduled update in 30m.

sana: Thanks everyone. I'll document commands and timeline in the incident ticket.

deepa: Adding notes to runbook and creating follow-up ticket: "kv-cache: refine eviction + hot-prefix detection".

mike: Postmortem volunteers: sana, deepa, ryan, mike. I'll draft initial timeline.

clarence: Good work.

oncall-bot: Incident closed for pager rotation; thread will remain for postmortem discussion."
